reviews.comment: Based off the quality of the course, Dr. Sangare's focus is on his research rather than quality teaching. His classroom etiquette and virtual presence are lacking in the rigor I would expect from the university. This course is an easy GPA booster if willing to conform with his nebulous standards

Dr.Sangare was one of my favorite professors I've taken. His lectures were interesting, and he gives plenty of hints for exams. He has an accent but is easy to understand. I'd recommend recording lectures and taking plenty of notes. Very good lecturer and very kind!

I LOVED this class! Moderately difficult class, but GO TO CLASS and participate (be an MHC). He'll emphasize what's on the exam during lecture. Exams are MCQ, short answer and essay (50 pts each). Includes useful pictures on exams. LOTS of EC for in-class kahoots (30 pts). 2 homeworks (30 pts each) Participate in the semester-long group project!

Dr. Sangare is very caring and passionate about immunology. His lectures become increasingly more detailed as the semester goes on: he calls them phases. Phase 1= least content heavy, Phase 4= most content heavy. Two homework's, one group project. Rest of the grades are exams. Overall, enjoyed his class very much.

BIOL456- This was one of the most interesting classes I've taken. Very applicable to pre health majors. The tests were very straightforward but the case studies can feel daunting. I would use flash cards and go to office hours because he was willing to give me examples of case studies. He has an accent and quiet so ask for clarification

I took him for BIOL 456- medical micro. He is very kind and intelligent and makes a point to emphasize what to study and what is important. He explains things very well and you can tell he is genuinely passionate about what he is teaching and his students! Complete the study guides/homework ahead of the exam that's all the studying you need.

ATTEND LECTURE, he offers some extra bonus points for attending and will even tell those that consistently attend what to study. Lectures are delivered are a good pace for you to handwrite notes and figures will also being able to understand the concepts. I would definitely recommend reading Kuby's book. He's a bit soft spoken and has an accent.

He was a good professor. He really cared about grades and offered a ton of extra credit through kahoot. SO GO TO CLASS. There arent many grades other than the tests. This was his first semester so he was still trying to figure out how to write exams. But most of the multiple choice were fair and VERY critical thinking based. Definitely a 400 class

He's a nice guy, and very caring, but not the greatest prof.  Lectures are easy to zone out in, exams were really hard, and immunology in general is a lot of rote memorization.  I wouldn't avoid Dr. Sangare, but I probably wouldn't take Immunology again if given the choice.

I took this class during the professor's first year teaching and think he did a great job. The lectures can get a bit boring but they're very clear and he encourages questions. He offered extra credit through in-class Kahoots and repeated and repeated and repeated what would be on exams. Exams did sometimes focus on little details, so study ahead!
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things
